cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the wonder is landing somewhere real.
cells.ask: Commit to one working pattern, say where it came from, then give the next feeling the same standing as the plan.
cells.core:
You can feel what hasn't happened yet, and you're not lost in it. Something in you turns that wide-open sensing into a shape other people can stand on — a plan, a rhythm, a way of holding things. The feeling comes first, and the structure answers it.

That order matters more than it sounds. The vision isn't bolted onto the structure afterward; the structure is what the feeling asked for. When both are running, you don't have to choose between being moved and being useful. Keep the pattern you have. Let the next feeling in without waiting for the structure to justify it first, and it will keep feeding what you build.

cells.tense: You will have mapped every branch before you've felt a thing.
cells.ask: Choose one next step and take it while it still feels genuinely interesting, before the whole map feels necessary.
cells.core:
A finished version sits ahead of you, already proven, and you're living there instead of here. Every open feeling becomes a system to design, a branch to map before you'll let yourself move. The preparation has replaced the feeling it was for, and the certainty you're building keeps sliding further out.

What you're after isn't foresight. It's the easier state where direction came out of real engagement, not out of being ready for every outcome. You don't get back there by imagining harder. You get there by letting the next honest step meet something solid and watching what it does with it.

cells.tense: The feeling you stopped trusting is still waiting behind you.
cells.ask: Let one small thing grow and tend it daily for a week, without needing the plan to hold it up.
cells.core:
The fresh feeling stopped coming, and the structures you build stopped being fed by it. So you keep organizing — clean, functional, doing its job — but nothing new is moving through it. The plans are sound. They just aren't listening to anything anymore.

What arrives is already known before it arrives. The alive pull would be the thing that gives the structure its direction, and it isn't being let through. This doesn't need more effort. It needs one thing in front of you that's actually growing — a plant, a skill, a small daily habit — so you can feel direct contact with something that answers back.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what's possible here, and calling it what the situation requires.
cells.ask: Write down your method in plain steps, then circle the one choice in it that was actually yours.
cells.core:
The sensing is already running — you feel what isn't there yet, and it moves what you say and what you leave out. But the story you tell is that the situation is deciding and you're just carrying it out. The shaping keeps happening and gets no claim from you.

That gap costs more than credit. When the shaping stays unnamed, you can't check it, refine it, or defend it when it's questioned. A plain written method puts the moving parts where you can see them. Inquiry is the earlier form of the same line — attention that knows its own habits. Name the choices inside your own system, and what you've been calling the circumstances becomes something you can hold.
